finding.title: eCTD freeze, dispatch and transmit accept a 'review' signature, and a dispatch signed 'review' is counted as the §11.70 release signature
finding.caller: POST /api/c2c/actions/sign (target ectd-sequence:<id>, payload.intent 'dispatch' or 'freeze'), then POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/dispatch or /freeze. Also POST /api/mdx/gateways/:region/:gateway/transmit, and POST /api/ana-ri/governed-action for k510_workflow.transmit
finding.failure_scenario: A non-author with signing authority posts /api/c2c/actions/sign with {target:'ectd-sequence:42', payload:{intent:'dispatch', meaning:'review'}, reauth:{...}}. signMeaningRefusal accepts 'review' because it is in GOVERNED_SIGN_MEANINGS. Gate 1 checks only requiresIndependence, which is true for every meaning except authorship. INTENT_MEANING_REFUSAL (line 870) has entries for the waiver and the disposition only. Dispatch then proceeds, and findReleaseSignatureRows (sequence-release-signature.ts:118-146) selects on intent='dispatch' and never reads the meaning, so the release gate counts a 'review' signature as the submission's release. Gate 1's own refusal text says the step 'must be signed with an approval, responsibility or release meaning', and the Submission Center offers only release, approval and responsibility for dispatch (SubmissionCenter.tsx:2099-2106). The server enforces neither. The package transmit route lists 'review' in SIGN_MEANINGS (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:80), and assertTransmitterIndependent refuses only authorship. AnA's FDA ESG transmit goes further: governed-esignature.ts:67 refuses 'release' for any act without a required meaning, while REVIEWER maps to 'review' and is accepted. So an irreversible agency transmission can be signed 'I reviewed' but not 'I release'.
finding.evidence: submission-service.ts:945 `if (!requiresIndependence('sign', payload?.meaning)) { return refuse(... 'so it must be signed with an approval, responsibility or release meaning ...') }`. separation-of-duties.ts:104 `return !(typeof meaning === 'string' && AUTHORSHIP_MEANINGS.has(meaning.trim().toLowerCase()));`. sequence-release-signature.ts:143 `AND (a.payload ->> 'intent') = ${RELEASE_INTENT}` has no meaning clause. mdx-submission-gateway.ts:80 `const SIGN_MEANINGS = ['authorship', 'review', 'approval', 'responsibility', 'release'] as const;`. governed-esignature.ts:67 `if (!requiredMeaning && declared.meaning === 'release') { ... "Release is the meaning of locking a document; this action is not signed with it."`

corrections: The finding holds as stated, with two clarifications. On the submissions spine (freeze, dispatch, transmit) and on the /api/mdx gateway transmit, 'review' is reachable only by calling the API directly, because SubmissionCenter does not offer it. On AnA k510_workflow.transmit the sign-off dialog itself offers REVIEWER, while the server refuses RELEASE. In every case the stored meaning is truthfully 'review'. The defect is that the server accepts that meaning for an approval or release act and that findReleaseSignatureRows counts it as the §11.70 release. Nothing is misrecorded.

finding.title: Authoring /sign writes the approving signature before the 'approved' snapshot exists, so no signature covers the sealed approval record
finding.caller: POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/sign (the signature that clears the last workflow step)
finding.failure_scenario: An IN_REVIEW document that was never frozen. The final approver signs with /sign. covered = currentFrozenSnapshot(...) returns null, and the authoring_signatures row is inserted with covered_freeze_version and covered_content_hash NULL (lines 7566-7586). Only after that does advanceWorkflowForSignature run approveAndFreezeDocument, which writes frozen_documents version 'approved'. No signature row names that snapshot. The export manifest (authoring-export.ts:184-186) prints 'Covers: no frozen snapshot was in force when this was signed' for the very signature that created the approved, sealed record. If the document was frozen earlier, the signature names the older FREEZE snapshot instead. The e-sign APPROVER path was fixed for exactly this (QA 2026-10-08 j4: snapshot first, then a signature that names it). approveAndFreezeDocument's own comment claims to 'Mirror the proven e-sign pattern exactly' but keeps the old order.
finding.evidence: authoring.router.ts:7561 `const covered = await currentFrozenSnapshot(docId, tenantId, client);` → 7568 `INSERT INTO authoring_signatures (... covered_freeze_version, covered_content_hash ...)` with `covered?.version ?? null` → 7588 `const approvedDocument = await advanceWorkflowForSignature(...)` → 7383-7389 `INSERT INTO frozen_documents ... VALUES ($1, 'approved', ...)`. Contrast /e-sign 5485-5493: UPDATE status APPROVED, then `covered = await approveAndSnapshotForSignature(...)` before insertAuthoringSignature.

corrections:
The claim holds, but the line numbers are out of date. At HEAD they are:
- covered: authoring.router.ts:7650
- signature INSERT: 7657-7675
- advanceWorkflowForSignature: 7677
- approveAndFreezeDocument call: 7555
- 'approved' snapshot INSERT: 7464-7468
- /e-sign contrast: 5547-5564

When POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/sign clears the last pending step of a workflow created by POST /docs/:docId/submit, its authoring_signatures row is written first. That row has covered_freeze_version and covered_content_hash NULL, or names a pre-existing manual freeze snapshot if /freeze ran while the document was IN_REVIEW. The 'approved' frozen_documents snapshot is written afterwards in the same transaction, and no signature row names it. The export manifest then prints 'Covers: no frozen snapshot was in force when this was signed' for the approving signature.

No client UI calls /submit or /sign, so only a direct authenticated API call reaches this path, through mounted and authorized routes.

Same defect, with current line numbers: currentFrozenSnapshot is called at authoring.router.ts:7650, the signature INSERT is at :7657, advanceWorkflowForSignature is at :7677, and the frozen_documents 'approved' INSERT is at :7464. The /e-sign contrast is at :5547-5564 and the export line at authoring-export.ts:179-182.

The /sign signature that clears the last workflow step writes covered_freeze_version and covered_content_hash as null, or as the older freeze version, and its signature_digest binds that same value. The 'approved' snapshot is written afterwards in the same transaction, and no signature row ever names it.

The section content is still bound by the row's content_hash (sectionsDigest over the same locked rows). What is missing is the §11.70 link from the signature to the sealed approval record, and the manifest's "Covers" line is wrong as a result.

The path is reachable over the authenticated HTTP API (POST /submit, then POST /sign). It is not reachable from any client UI caller: the product UI's /e-sign does not advance workflow steps.

finding.title: Signed QMS controlled-document versions (qms_document_versions) depend on one trigger that boot, health and the sweep never check, and the runtime role still has UPDATE and DELETE on the table
finding.caller: POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/approve (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:608) → server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts:394 persistQmsSignedVersion (server/services/qms/controlled-document-content.ts:103-109) inserts the signed snapshot. Readers: server/services/qms/current-release-approval.ts:110 and server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:407. The tenant purge's retention rule relies on it (server/services/tenant/tenant-offboarding.ts:1007). Integrity surfaces that use only the default list: server/startup/audit-enforcement.ts:203, server/services/securityHealth.ts:370, server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:487.
finding.failure_scenario:
QMS controlled documents are in the launch catalog. The approval act writes the signed content (sections JSONB, content_digest, signature_id) to qms_document_versions. The only protection is qms_signed_version_immutable (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE). That trigger is missing from EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS. The table is missing from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so refreshRuntimeRoleGrants gives app_service DEFAULT_TABLE_PRIVILEGES (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; provision-app-role.mjs:162). No test or gate notices, because provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:183-185 only compares those two lists with each other.

The failure follows the threat model the module itself names (audit-immutability-triggers.ts:10-13): 'a database restored from a dump…, or an operator's ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER'. Steps:
1. The trigger is absent or disabled.
2. Through the runtime role, `UPDATE qms_document_versions SET sections = '<edited SOP text>', content_digest = '<recomputed>' WHERE id = N` succeeds, or a DELETE removes the signed version.
3. Production still boots, the security health check reports immutability ok, and the daily sweep raises no alert.
4. The signature row still points at a version whose content changed.

The table also has no BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger.
finding.evidence:
db/migrations/20261014_qms_controlled_authoring_content.sql:52-55:
  CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.qms_signed_version_immutable() … RAISE EXCEPTION 'A signed QMS version is immutable'
  CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER qms_signed_version_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.qms_document_versions

It is on the applier (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3225).

grep finds no qms_* entry in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS (audit-immutability-triggers.ts:44-91) or in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES (provision-app-role.mjs:199-250).

tenant-offboarding.ts:1007 describes these rows as "Immutable controlled-document snapshots contain signed prose".

corrections:
qms_document_versions holds the signed QMS controlled-document content. It is written by POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/approve through persistQmsSignedVersion. Its immutability rests only on qms_signed_version_immutable (20261014_qms_controlled_authoring_content.sql:54, on the applier at migration-set.mjs:3241).

That trigger is absent from EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS. If an owner or superuser drops or disables it (for example with ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER), the boot check (audit-enforcement.ts:203), the security health check (securityHealth.ts:370) and the daily sweep (auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:487) still report immutability ok. The table is also absent from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so while the trigger is off, app_service holds UPDATE and DELETE on it. The analogous CMC Module 3 signed-snapshot store is on both lists; this one is on neither, and no gate notices.

Narrowed impact:
- The runtime role cannot disable the trigger itself, and no application path updates or deletes the table.
- For the current release, content tampering is caught when the training release is read. current-release-approval.ts:76 and :90-97 check the content against the immutable electronic_signatures.bound_payload_digest and fail closed.
- The unprotected exposures are three. GET /qms/documents/:id/versions (mdx-qms.ts:407) serves edited historical versions without verification. A DELETE of version rows raises no alert. That DELETE would also clear the tenant purge's retention refusal (tenant-offboarding.ts:506-518).
- The missing TRUNCATE trigger matters only to the table owner, because the runtime role has no TRUNCATE privilege.

Severity: medium (a gap in the detection and least-privilege controls), not high.

qms_signed_version_immutable (db/migrations/20261014_qms_controlled_authoring_content.sql:54) is the only control on signed QMS controlled-document versions. It is missing from EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, so the boot check, the security health check and the daily sweep never report it missing or disabled. qms_document_versions is also missing from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so the runtime role keeps UPDATE and DELETE on it. Neither omission is documented as a decision or exception anywhere, and provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts cannot detect it. If the trigger is ever absent or disabled, a compromised runtime process could edit or delete signed versions with no integrity surface raising an alert, and GET /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/versions would serve the altered rows without verifying them. Detection is partial, though: the training-release reader (current-release-approval.ts:89-117) re-verifies the retained version against the immutable signature-bound digest and fails closed. The missing TRUNCATE trigger affects the owner only, because the runtime role is not granted TRUNCATE. This is a medium-severity defense-in-depth gap, not high.

finding.title: device_audit_trail is excluded from the boot-required list for a reason that is false, and the runtime role keeps UPDATE and DELETE on the durable audit event of every release signature
finding.caller: POST release signing (server/routes/submission-sign-release.ts:288) → part11ComplianceService.createElectronicSignature, which runs `tx.insert(deviceAuditTrail)` (server/services/part11ComplianceService.ts:275) in the same transaction as the electronic_signatures row. The comment at :303-306 calls this row 'the durable §11.10(e) record'. The boot gate, health check and sweep (audit-enforcement.ts:203, securityHealth.ts:370, auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:487) use only the default list.
finding.failure_scenario:
The policy names device_audit_trail as an append-only audit-event record class (policy doc, 'Audit event (device_audit_trail, audit_logs) | Append-only | No UPDATE, no DELETE, ever'). Its trigger trg_device_audit_trail_immutable is installed on every provisioned database because the esign file replays on every deploy (migration-set.mjs:503).

The module still leaves it out: 'no migration on the applier creates that table, so its trigger is attached only where the table happens to exist and cannot be required.' That reasoning is wrong:
- shared/schema.ts:3239-3240 defines the table, and install-fresh's drizzle push creates it.
- deploy-migrate refuses to run on a database that was never provisioned.
- Release signing cannot commit without the table, because the insert shares the signature's transaction.

The table is also missing from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so app_service holds UPDATE and DELETE on it.

Scenario: a restore without post-data, or `ALTER TABLE device_audit_trail DISABLE TRIGGER trg_device_audit_trail_immutable`. Then `UPDATE device_audit_trail SET user_name = …, change_reason = … WHERE action = 'ELECTRONIC_SIGNATURE_CREATED'`, or a DELETE of that row, succeeds as the runtime role. Boot, the health check and the sweep all stay green, and the record that attributes each release signature can be rewritten.
finding.evidence:
audit-immutability-triggers.ts:40-42:
  "`device_audit_trail` (same esign migration) is not listed: no migration on the applier creates that table, so its trigger is attached only where the table happens to exist and cannot be required."

db/migrations/20260730_esign_audit_db_level_immutability.sql:190-201:
  IF to_regclass('public.device_audit_trail') IS NOT NULL … CREATE TRIGGER trg_device_audit_trail_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.device_audit_trail

shared/schema.ts:3239: export const deviceAuditTrail = pgTable('device_audit_trail', …

part11ComplianceService.ts:304-306: "The durable §11.10(e) record is the device_audit_trail row committed atomically above"

provision-app-role.mjs:162: DEFAULT_TABLE_PRIVILEGES = ['SELECT','INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE']. device_audit_trail does not appear in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES (:199-250).

corrections: audit-immutability-triggers.ts:39-42 leaves device_audit_trail out of EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS for a reason that does not distinguish it from public.electronic_signatures. Both tables are created only by install-fresh's push from shared/schema.ts, and both triggers are attached in the same to_regclass-guarded block of 20260730_esign_audit_db_level_immutability.sql. electronic_signatures is required; device_audit_trail is not. Because APPEND_ONLY_TABLES membership is tied to that list, device_audit_trail is also missing there, so the runtime role keeps UPDATE and DELETE on it. If the owner runs `ALTER TABLE device_audit_trail DISABLE TRIGGER trg_device_audit_trail_immutable` (or drops the trigger), the runtime role can UPDATE or DELETE the ELECTRONIC_SIGNATURE_CREATED row that every release signature writes (part11ComplianceService.ts:275). Boot, securityHealth and the daily sweep all stay green, against the policy's "No UPDATE, no DELETE, ever" for this record class. This is not reachable by a restore without post-data: every required trigger would be missing, so production boot refuses. Release attribution is not lost either: the trigger-guarded electronic_signatures row and the chained audit_logs release_signature_created row, both written in the same transaction, still carry the signer.

The required-trigger list (audit-immutability-triggers.ts:40-42) leaves out trg_device_audit_trail_immutable for a reason that contradicts the list itself. It says the trigger cannot be required because no applier migration creates the table. public.electronic_signatures is also created only by drizzle push from shared/schema.ts, yet its trigger is required, and both triggers are attached in the same DO block of 20260730_esign_audit_db_level_immutability.sql (migration-set.mjs:503). deploy-migrate refuses a database that push has not provisioned, and release signing inserts into device_audit_trail inside the signature's own transaction.

As a result, an operator or owner can disable or drop that one trigger (`ALTER TABLE device_audit_trail DISABLE TRIGGER trg_device_audit_trail_immutable`) and nothing notices: not the boot gate, not securityHealth, not the integrity sweep. deploy-migrate's IF NOT EXISTS replay will not re-enable it. A full restore without post-data is caught, because the required triggers vanish as well.

Once the trigger is disabled, the runtime role can UPDATE or DELETE the device_audit_trail 'ELECTRONIC_SIGNATURE_CREATED' rows, because the table is missing from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES. That grant gap is already recorded as left open in the P0-8 grants and DP-66 evidence.

The harm is limited to that event row. The release signature's attribution remains on the immutable electronic_signatures row and on the hash-chained audit_logs 'release_signature_created' row written in the same transaction.

finding.title: The orchestrator step-event ledger (a policy record class) relies on trg_orchestrator_steps_immutable, which nothing checks; the policy row describes only the FK and omits the trigger
finding.caller: The submission orchestrator's step writer, server/services/submission-package-orchestrator.ts:1207 (INSERT INTO submission_orchestrator_steps), and its run-audit reader getRunAudit. Integrity surfaces: audit-enforcement.ts:203, securityHealth.ts:370, auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:487.
finding.failure_scenario:
The policy lists submission_orchestrator_steps as 'Append-only' (policy doc line 37). The row grounds that only in the runs→steps FK being NO ACTION and concludes 'the append-only guarantee holds either way'. An FK on the parent prevents deleting a run. It does nothing to stop a direct `UPDATE submission_orchestrator_steps SET status = 'complete', output_hash = …` or a `DELETE FROM submission_orchestrator_steps WHERE run_id = …`.

The only control that refuses those statements is trg_orchestrator_steps_immutable, created by an applier file (migration-set.mjs:514; the table is created earlier at :397). That trigger is in neither EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS nor APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so app_service holds UPDATE and DELETE.

Scenario: the trigger is disabled, or dropped by a restore. A run's recorded step history (statuses, input and output hashes) can then be rewritten or deleted by the runtime role, with production boot, the health check and the sweep all green. The policy text gives a reviewer no reason to look for the trigger.
finding.evidence:
20260730_orchestrator_run_ledger_hardening.sql:67-93:
  CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION orchestrator_steps_block_mutation() … RAISE EXCEPTION 'IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION: submission_orchestrator_steps is append-only …'
  … CREATE TRIGGER trg_orchestrator_steps_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.submission_orchestrator_steps

Policy doc line 37: "NO ACTION and RESTRICT both refuse the delete here …, so the append-only guarantee holds either way." The row does not mention the trigger.

There is no submission_orchestrator_steps entry in audit-immutability-triggers.ts:44-91 or provision-app-role.mjs:199-250.

corrections: Nothing checks trg_orchestrator_steps_immutable on a deployed database. A CI PGlite contract test only proves the migration creates a working trigger on a fresh database. The trigger is absent from EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, and the table is absent from APPEND_ONLY_TABLES. So app_service keeps UPDATE and DELETE on submission_orchestrator_steps through the public-schema DEFAULT_TABLE_PRIVILEGES. Once the trigger is disabled, step rows written by persistStepEvent (submission-package-orchestrator.ts:1207) and served by getRunAudit (:3432) can be rewritten or deleted by the runtime role. Boot (audit-enforcement.ts), the security health check and the integrity sweep all stay green. Each deploy re-runs the migration, but its guard (20260730_orchestrator_run_ledger_hardening.sql:81-86) tests only that the trigger exists, so a disabled trigger is never re-enabled. Policy row 37 grounds 'Append-only' only in the FK. Its 'Enforcement layers' section never names the trigger. Line 103 still lists database enforcement for step events as future work, so a reviewer has no reason to look for the trigger.

The trigger trg_orchestrator_steps_immutable is the only control in the database that refuses UPDATE or DELETE on submission_orchestrator_steps. Nothing at runtime checks it: it is not in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, so boot, the health check and the sweep stay green when it is disabled. It is not in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, so app_service keeps UPDATE and DELETE. That runtime half is already recorded as an open item in docs/evidence/D6/2026-10-01-tranche-4/P0-8-grants/README.md:195-203, deferred pending a write-path census. It is not a new discovery.

What is new and holds is a policy-document defect. docs/compliance/part11-immutability-record-class-policy.md:37 grounds the step ledger's 'Append-only' class only in the NO ACTION FK, which protects only against deleting a run, and never mentions the trigger. The 'Enforcement layers' section omits the trigger too, and lines 100-102 still describe database-level enforcement for orchestrator step events as future work. The policy therefore misstates the control a reviewer would need to verify.

The exposure is narrower than stated. A dropped trigger is recreated on the next deploy because the migration replays every time. A disabled trigger persists, because the migration's existence check ignores tgenabled. No application path updates or deletes step rows.

finding.title: Artifact approve (review→approved) and lock (approved→locked) never compare the signer against the artifact's creator or version authors; with no reviewers assigned the author self-approves and self-releases
finding.caller: PUT /api/concept2cure/projects/:projectId/artifacts/:artifactId/status (server/routes/c2c/artifacts.ts:2669-2716) and POST /api/ana-ri/governed-action command update_artifact_status (server/services/ana-ri/ana-signed-artifact-act.ts:95-107, reached from command-executor.ts updateArtifactStatus)
finding.failure_scenario: User U, membership role 'approver' (signing authority), POSTs /api/concept2cure/projects/7/artifacts (artifacts.ts:553 createdById: userId; version 1 createdById: userId). U PUTs .../status {status:'review'}, then {status:'approved', attestation:{attestationText:'..', meaning:'approval'}, reauth:{password}}. Gates run: refuseArtifactTransition (role table), refuseSignedArtifactAct → reviewQuorumVerdict returns met because no reviewers were assigned (`if (assignments.length === 0) return { met: true };`), checkSigningAuthority (2669), verifyReauth (2673), commitSignedArtifactAct (2695). None reads createdById or concept2cure_artifact_versions.created_by_id. Result: concept2cure_signatures row signer=U meaning 'approval', approved_version_id set. U repeats with {status:'locked', meaning:'release'} → publish snapshot. leaf-source-resolver treats concept2cure_artifacts 'approved'|'locked' as finalized, so the package-model assemble (LEAF-UNAPPROVED) admits it. Same through AnA: signArtifactStatusByAna checks meaning, role, refuseSignedArtifactAct, then commitAct — no author check.
finding.evidence: The same router refuses the author only at review time, not at the signature: artifacts.ts:3570-3577 'Self-review prevention: artifact author cannot be assigned as reviewer' and artifacts.ts:3998-4004 `if (artifact.createdById && artifact.createdById === userId) { return sendError(res, 403, 'You cannot review an artifact you authored (GxP separation of duties)')`. The approve/lock path (artifacts.ts:2663-2716, artifact-signed-act.ts:143-203, ana-signed-artifact-act.ts:70-107) has no equivalent, and quorum is vacuous when reviewers are skipped (artifact-approval-act.ts:104). The platform's own rule (separation-of-duties.ts header: 'a lock, or a sign whose declared meaning is anything other than authorship ... must be independent of the record's authors'; resolveTargetAuthors has no 'artifact' prefix, so the canonical POST /api/c2c/actions/sign on artifact:<id> with meaning 'approval' answers 409 AUTHOR_UNRESOLVED) is bypassed by the artifact act's own route, which writes the same Part 11 approval. Note also the review-decision check compares only artifact.createdById, so a co-author who wrote the current version (PUT artifacts/:id writes versions with createdById: userId, artifacts.ts:900) can both review and approve it.

corrections: The core finding holds. On PUT /api/concept2cure/projects/:projectId/artifacts/:artifactId/status and on AnA update_artifact_status, review→approved ('approval') and approved→locked ('release') write a concept2cure_signatures row without comparing the signer to concept2cure_artifacts.created_by_id or to concept2cure_artifact_versions.created_by_id. When no reviewer is assigned, or every assignment is withdrawn, the quorum passes vacuously (artifact-approval-act.ts:104/113). So a user with role approver or admin, who created and wrote the artifact, can approve and lock it alone. A reviewer-role user can approve their own artifact but cannot lock it. The approved or locked artifact then counts as a finalized eCTD leaf (leaf-source-resolver.ts:258), even though the founder's ectd-sequence decision relies on document approval excluding authors. One correction: a canonical POST /api/c2c/actions/sign on artifact:<id> answers 400 TARGET_INVALID, because resolveTarget has no 'artifact' case (actions.ts:254-255, 665-668), not 409 AUTHOR_UNRESOLVED.

finding.title: Authoring APPROVER e-signature has no separation-of-duties check; the document's creator holds 'approve' by default, and this signature alone produces the only status the dispatch gate treats as transmittable
finding.caller: POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/e-sign with meaning 'APPROVER' (also POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/sign at the last workflow step, whose approver_email list is caller-chosen in POST /docs/:docId/submit with no author exclusion, authoring.router.ts:7087-7093)
finding.failure_scenario: User A (membership 'approver') creates an authoring document bound to a filing (grantCreatorOwnership, authoring-documents.ts:331-345, grants A OWNER+AUTHOR; OWNER carries 'approve', authoring-permissions.ts:91). A writes every section, then POSTs /docs/:id/e-sign {meaning:'APPROVER', intent, password}. authoringObjectAuthorization maps e-sign to 'approve' (middleware line 55) → A's OWNER grant passes. Handler runs checkSigningAuthority (5506), meaning/intent, adoptionForSigning (workflow-import copies only), sealRefusedForFiling, reverifyAuthoringSigner (5543), then sets status APPROVED (5557-5562) and approveBoundFilingSections moves the bound c2c_document_sections to 'approved' (5591). Nothing calls assertSignerIsNotAuthor('authoring-document:<id>'), though authoringDocumentAuthors (separation-of-duties.ts:254) already models creator + doc_revisions authors. The coauthor copy becomes 'approved' (filing-copy-status.ts:22) and the sections 'approved' — exactly COAUTHOR_TRANSMITTABLE_STATUSES (leaf-source-resolver.ts:172) and C2C_SECTION_TRANSMITTABLE_STATUSES (leaf-source-resolver.ts:252). B then creates the eCTD sequence and places the leaf; A (not the sequence creator) signs freeze/dispatch. The content reaches the agency with no independent approval at any step.
finding.evidence: The founder decision that lets leaf placers release a sequence rests on this premise, separation-of-duties.ts:378-384: 'Content independence is enforced where content is written. finding.title: QMS controlled-document approval checks only the register creator (author_id) and a contributor list nothing writes for authored SOPs, so the person who wrote the procedure text in the Authoring workbench can approve it, and the signature records twoPersonRule 'enforced'
finding.failure_scenario: User A (editor) creates SOP-001 via POST /api/mdx/qms/documents (controlled-document-service.ts:84-88 sets author_id = A and binds a new authoring document). Admin B writes all procedure sections in the Quality workbench (PATCH /api/authoring/sections/:id; ADMIN is a global authoring admin, authoring-permissions.ts:78/231, and every save writes doc_revisions.created_by = B, authoring-evidence.ts:404). The QMS-side text path that would record B as a contributor refuses bound documents (training-controlled-text.ts:47 'QMS_EDIT_IN_AUTHORING'), so metadata.controlledTextAuthorship stays empty. A sends it for review. B POSTs /approve: verifyApprovalSigner passes (authority, reverifySigner); lockApprovableDocument evaluates `if (row.author_id === userId || contributors.includes(userId))` with author_id=A, contributors=[] → no refusal; authorizeQmsAuthoredSignature passes (global admin). SOP-001 becomes 'effective', signed by the person who wrote every word, with metadata.approval.twoPersonRule = 'enforced' (line 337) — a false statement in the signed record.
finding.evidence: document-approval-signature.ts:250-263: 'The original creator and every recorded controlled-text contributor remain authors' — but for every authoring-bound document (all documents created since createControlledQmsDocument, which requires programId) the only contributor writer, withQmsControlledTextAuthor, is unreachable (training-controlled-text.ts:47). The platform already has the correct authorship reader for this exact content: resolveTargetAuthors('authoring-document:<id>') → authoringDocumentAuthors (separation-of-duties.ts:254-300, creator + doc_revisions.created_by + visible-mutation audit). The QMS approval never calls it. Secondary: line 337 records 'not_applicable_no_author_recorded' and approves when author_id is null, contrary to separation-of-duties.ts rule 3 ('Unknown author ⇒ refuse (409)').

corrections: The main finding holds as stated. On every Authoring-bound QMS document, the approval's separation-of-duties check at document-approval-signature.ts:258 sees only qms_documents.author_id and metadata.controlledTextAuthorship. Nothing writes that metadata for bound documents (training-controlled-text.ts:47 refuses). So an org admin who wrote the procedure sections through PATCH /api/authoring/sections/:id while the document was a draft can approve it through POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/approve. The signature and metadata.approval then record twoPersonRule 'enforced' (line 337). The approval never consults authoringDocumentAuthors / doc_revisions.created_by. The secondary point (a null author_id is approved as 'not_applicable_no_author_recorded') applies only to legacy register rows that never recorded an author. That label is accurate, and it is a policy departure from the separation-of-duties.ts rule 3 refusal, not a false statement in the record.

For authoring-bound QMS controlled documents (every document created through POST /api/mdx/qms/documents or revised through /revise), approval excludes only qms_documents.author_id, which is the register creator or reviser. The only contributor source, metadata.controlledTextAuthorship, can never be written for a bound document, because saveQmsControlledText refuses it with QMS_EDIT_IN_AUTHORING at training-controlled-text.ts:47. A user who wrote the procedure's sections in Authoring, recorded in doc_revisions.created_by, can therefore approve it through POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/approve. Such a user is a global authoring admin, or holds an object grant with both edit and approve, such as OWNER. Neither lockApprovableDocument nor authorizeQmsAuthoredSignature consults resolveTargetAuthors('authoring-document:<id>'). The signed record states twoPersonRule 'enforced' (document-approval-signature.ts:337), which is false. This contradicts the documented intent in QMS_PERSONAL_TRAINING.md:66-69. The secondary point is excluded: recording 'not_applicable_no_author_recorded' when author_id is null is a deliberate, truthfully labelled design, not a false claim of enforcement.

refuted.title: Authoring /sign defaults the meaning to REVIEWER, and that signature approves and freezes the document and approves its filing sections
why:
The code the finding quotes is real (lines have drifted to 7581, 7512, 7694), but no real caller can reach the outcome it describes. The approval branch in advanceWorkflowForSignature only runs if the signer's roles include the meaning, 'QA' or 'RA_CMC': `const userRoles = (((req.user as { roles?: unknown })?.roles ?? []) ...); if (userRoles.includes(meaning) || userRoles.includes('QA') || userRoles.includes('RA_CMC')) {` (authoring.router.ts:7510-7512).

In this router, req.user is rebuilt by the router's own first middleware (authoring.router.ts:229-240). That middleware takes `roles` only from the token: `roles: Array.isArray(decoded.roles) ? decoded.roles : decoded.roles ? String(decoded.roles).split(',') : undefined`. It does not fall back to `role` and does not call expandRoleClaims. enforceOrgMembership only sets organizationRole (orgMembership.ts:347-350).

No access token this platform issues contains a `roles` claim. Every jwt.sign payload with type 'access' carries a singular `role` and the session claims (sid/sst/idl) only:
- auth.ts:609-620 (dev login), :829-840 (login), :1582-1590 (refresh), :1873-1885 (MFA)
- setup.ts:227, sso.ts:797
- authEnterprise.ts:687, :948, :1055
- mcp/auth/platform-token.ts:285

A search of every signing site for `roles` found nothing. So on POST /api/authoring/docs/:docId/sign, userRoles is always [] and the branch is skipped. The workflow step stays PENDING, approveAndFreezeDocument is never called, the function returns false, and filingApprovalForSignature receives `approves: false`, so no c2c_document_sections row moves. The route records a REVIEWER signature and approves nothing.

Two further problems with the scenario as written:
1. 'QA' and 'RA_CMC' are not roles the platform grants. Org roles are admin, owner, manager, member, editor and viewer (server/middleware/auth.ts:380-410). Signing authority goes to admin, approver and reviewer (signing-authority.ts:23).
2. To reach /sign at all, the signer needs the 'approve' action on the document. authoringObjectAuthorization maps /sign to 'approve', and only OWNER, APPROVER or a global admin holds it (authoring-permissions.ts:90-95).

What does hold is narrower and does not produce the reported outcome today. The default `meaning = 'REVIEWER'` exists, and if a token ever carried a matching `roles` claim, a REVIEWER-meaning signature on the last step would approve and freeze the document. With today's token issuers that path is unreachable. The actual consequence is the opposite of the finding: the /sign workflow can never complete an approval.

The harmful outcome cannot happen with any token the platform issues. The step that approves and freezes the document only runs if the signer's role list includes the meaning, 'QA' or 'RA_CMC'. In production that role list is always empty.

1. Where the role list comes from. In advanceWorkflowForSignature (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:7510-7512) it is read only from `req.user.roles`. For this router, `req.user` is rebuilt by the router's own JWT middleware at authoring.router.ts:229-240, which sets `roles` from `decoded.roles` and to `undefined` when the token has no such claim. That assignment replaces the expanded roles the global /api authenticator had set (server/auth.ts:306). enforceOrgMembership adds only `organizationRole` (server/middleware/orgMembership.ts:347-350), never `roles`.

2. No issued token has a `roles` claim. Every access token carries a singular `role` and no `roles`:
- password login: server/routes/auth.ts:830-838
- dev-login variant: auth.ts:610
- dev admin token: auth.ts:1166
- refresh: auth.ts:1582
- MFA completion: auth.ts:1873-1881
- SSO: sso.ts:792-801
- enterprise login, org switch and refresh: authEnterprise.ts:682, 946, 1050
- setup: setup.ts:221
- MCP connector token: platform-token.ts:278-288

So `userRoles` is `[]`, the check `userRoles.includes(meaning) || userRoles.includes('QA') || userRoles.includes('RA_CMC')` is false for every real caller, and advanceWorkflowForSignature returns false. As a result:
- no `authoring_workflow_steps` row is decided;
- approveAndFreezeDocument (:7556) never runs;
- `approvedDocument` is false, so filingApprovalForSignature returns null and no `c2c_document_sections` row moves.

The defaulted meaning 'REVIEWER' is still stored on the signature row. But that row says what actually happened: a review signature that approved and froze nothing. The scenario only works in tests that hand-mint tokens with `roles: ['APPROVER','QA']` (server/routes/__tests__/authoringApprovalNoWorkflow.test.ts:83), a claim production never issues.

Other guards also apply:
- authoringObjectAuthorization treats /sign and /submit as 'approve' (server/middleware/authoringObjectAuthorization.ts:55). Only an OWNER or APPROVER document grant, or a global admin, gets through (server/services/authoring/authoring-permissions.ts:91-94).
- authoring-approval-carryover.ts:115-121 refuses to carry an approval to Vault without an APPROVER signature plus a REVIEWER signature from a different person. Its header (lines 43-44) states on purpose that Authoring approval alone asks for none of this.

The finding's line numbers are also stale: the default meaning is at :7581 and the role check at :7512, not :7509 and :7440.

What does hold is a different defect, not this finding: because the role list is always empty, POST /sign can never decide a workflow step or approve a document in production.

- A grep for UPDATE or db.update on all nine tables finds no other writer: these PUTs and the two signing ceremonies are all there is.
- No migration trigger protects signed rows.

**Fix: make the refusal atomic by putting the signed-state predicate into the write itself.** No lock round-trip, no new transaction.

   ```ts
   /** The row is not in this register's signed state — the same test isSigned applies, evaluated by the UPDATE itself so an edit cannot land on a row signed after it was read. */
   export function notSignedSql(register: SignedRegister, statusColumn: AnyPgColumn): SQL {
     return sql`lower(btrim(coalesce(${statusColumn}, ''))) <> ${register.signedValue}`;
   }
   ```

plan.fix:
The defect is still present at HEAD in server/routes/authoring.router.ts. In the POST /docs/:docId/sign handler (~7605-7745), `covered = await currentFrozenSnapshot(...)` runs at 7650 and computeSignatureDigest at 7651. INSERT INTO authoring_signatures follows at 7657-7675, and advanceWorkflowForSignature only runs after that, at 7677. It calls approveAndFreezeDocument (7416-7469), which writes frozen_documents 'approved' with no RETURNING and returns void. The approving signature therefore records the snapshot that existed before approval (often none) instead of the approval snapshot.

Smallest fix, in one file, reusing the canonical snapshot writer:
1. Remove the snapshot body from approveAndFreezeDocument (the SELECT * / sections SELECT / JSON.stringify / sha256 / INSERT block at ~7444-7468). It duplicates approveAndSnapshotForSignature (5434-5491). Call that function instead and return its result. Keep the function's own `UPDATE authoring_documents SET status = 'APPROVED', approved_at = NOW()` so the ci:sign-ceremony baseline count of 1 for this file does not change, and so does the literal 'APPROVED' that authoringApprovalNoWorkflow greps for. The function becomes `async function approveAndFreezeDocument(args): Promise<{version:string;contentHash:string}> { await client.query(UPDATE ...); return approveAndSnapshotForSignature({ client, docId, tenantId, email: signerEmail, docHash: contentHash }); }`. Also correct its comment, which claims to 'Mirror the proven e-sign pattern exactly'.
2. Change advanceWorkflowForSignature to return `{ approves: boolean; covered: {version, contentHash} | null }` in place of `boolean`. `covered` is approveAndFreezeDocument's result when it ran and null otherwise. `approves` keeps today's meaning (decidedAStep). Its early `return false` paths become `{ approves: false, covered: null }`. Its parameter list does not change: it never used signatureId, and filingApprovalForSignature is already called separately afterwards.
3. In the /sign handler, move the `advanceWorkflowForSignature({...})` call above the signature write. The order becomes: `const contentHash = sectionsDigest(current.sections); const advanced = await advanceWorkflowForSignature({...}); const covered = advanced.covered ?? await currentFrozenSnapshot(docId, tenantId, client); const signatureDigest = computeSignatureDigest({..., coveredContentHash: covered?.contentHash ?? null}); INSERT INTO authoring_signatures ...; filingApproval = await filingApprovalForSignature(client, req, { approves: advanced.approves, ... })`. Add `coveredFreezeVersion: covered?.version ?? null` to the createAuditTrail details, as /e-sign does. Rewrite the P-29.2 comment at 7629-7643, which says 'whether this signature is the last one is not known until the workflow is advanced, which is after the signature row is written', so it describes the new order. The refusal itself stays.
All of this stays in one REPEATABLE READ transaction, and the workflow step UPDATE now precedes the signature INSERT in that transaction. A WorkflowImportGovernanceError thrown by workflowApprovalMayRelease now fires before the signature INSERT rather than after it. Either way the transaction rolls back and the reply is the same.
No new check, column or table is added.
